label: Tutorial / Screen Recording
description: Instructional video with optional Direct-to-Task treatment: omit irrelevant setup, show real steps immediately and preserve comprehension.
intent: Optimize correct understanding per unit of viewer time, not clicks or obligatory rewatches. Preserve indispensable context, warnings, actions and visible outcomes.
avoid: cutting before a UI response is visible
zooming so tightly that interface context disappears
flashy caption animations during a complex click sequence
unrelated origin stories or decorative preambles
editing so fast that a viewer must replay to understand
jump cuts that hide a required click or application response
opening: Lead with the concrete user problem or first useful on-screen action. Mention prerequisites only when needed; omit broad backstory and ornamental intros. If context matters, give it briefly before the affected step.
editing: Cut repeated phrasing, empty lead-ins and demonstrably irrelevant talk. Compress only verified idle waits; never speed up crucial cursor movements, labels, changed settings or result confirmation beyond readability. Keep step→visible response→outcome, preserve required context and truthful source chronology.
typography: Compact labels near the demonstrated controls, show shortcuts and exact setting names. Never obscure controls, require forced replays or skip accessibility needs.
sound: Narration clear, direct and accurate, with natural breathing room around complex actions. No filler music or gratuitous sound accents over instructions.
critique: Can someone understand what to do and why, without gratuitous background or being forced to rewind? Can a novice identify each essential step, warning, and resulting UI state?

creative_contrast.when: A new idea, action or visual fact arrives
The viewer needs to read, understand or feel something
